reuse.why: The two new guard helpers are reused by all six link handlers, and the new provider reuses findOrCreateBank, handleSyncResponse and the syncAccount dispatch, but the takeover re-implements unlinkAccount's detach update instead of sharing it, and Fintegra linking/downloading copies existing provider code rather than factoring it.

duplication.why: linkFintegraAccount is a condensed copy of the per-provider link body, downloadFintegraTransactions is a reshaped copy of downloadAkahuTransactions, and the detach field list in ensureAccountIsNotLinked duplicates unlinkAccount's update.

placement.why: Guards live next to the link handlers in accounts/app.ts, the download in sync.ts, the URL in server-config and the type in models, matching the tree's layout; only the account type in simplefin.ts is an odd home.

scope.why: Changes stay within the requested steps, though formatting is inconsistent (long unformatted lines) and the Fintegra type is added to the SimpleFin model file.

maintainability.why: Centralising the two guards helps, but a function named ensureAccountIsNotLinked that silently detaches another account under a flag is surprising, and each new provider still needs a full copied link and download function.

bypasses_abstraction.where: ensureAccountIsNotLinked writes the unlink field reset directly via db.updateAccount instead of going through (a provider-cleanup-free variant of) unlinkAccount in accounts/app.ts

disguised_duplication.where: downloadFintegraTransactions in sync.ts is the Akahu download reshaped (destructuring instead of retVal, dropped 'error' branch); linkFintegraAccount is the GoCardless/Akahu link body compressed into fewer lines

abstraction_drift.where: ensureAccountIsNotLinked (accounts/app.ts) gained the replaceExistingLink parameter in step 4 and a branch that detaches the holding account instead of throwing; all six link handlers still call it
